verdict.summary: Getting a working OAuth connection for your own account is quick and needs no review. The only review step is for a Marketplace listing, which Notion says is a security review with a 5-10 business day reply, and public connections must be Any workspace scope to be listed.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1-2 hours for Gate 1 setup, plus token handling code (estimate, not from Notion docs). Marketplace listing adds drafting time and review wait.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Minutes after the public connection is created, if the authorization URL can be built (see blockers).
verdict.approval_wait: None to use an unlisted public connection through its OAuth flow. 5-10 business days for a Marketplace listing reply (review depth not stated).

gates.name: Works for you (development public connection, your own account)
gates.unlocks: You create a public connection, retrieve its client ID and secret, and authorize your own Notion account through the OAuth flow.
limits: Installation scope (Any workspace or Selected workspaces only) is set once at creation and cannot be changed afterward.
Notion's docs say the Authorization URL field populates only after the connection is submitted for review, so hosted-URL testing may not be possible before submission.
Notion's internal-connection page says Workspace Owner is required to create a connection; the public-connection page does not state this.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes once you can create connections.

gates.name: Invited/test users (no named tier in Notion docs)
gates.unlocks: Other members of test workspaces can authorize the connection. Each person authorizes individually.
limits: Each user who authorizes a public connection gets an individual token and must complete the flow individually.
Rate limits apply per connection: 180 requests per minute on non-Business plans, 600 per minute on Business and Enterprise, plus a shared per-workspace limit.
Notion's docs do not describe a test-user allowlist, user cap, or install cap. A third-party guide suggests keeping the development connection to test workspaces.
gates.time_to_reach: No Notion-documented review. Time depends on you inviting test users.

gates.name: Works for anyone (Marketplace listing, Any workspace only)
gates.unlocks: Your connection can be listed on the Notion Marketplace. Unlisted public connections can already be used through their OAuth flow without a listing.
limits: Only Any workspace public connections can be listed; Selected workspaces only connections are excluded.
Public connections must pass a Notion security review before Marketplace listing.
Rejections can be for brand or trademark issues, quality, or baseline criteria. You can revise and resubmit.
Marketplace review criteria beyond the FAQ (minimum installs, demo video, domain verification) are not stated in the findings.
gates.time_to_reach: Notion replies by email within 5-10 business days of submission. Security review timeline is not stated.

steps.title: Decide whether you need your own public connection
steps.detail: Composio lists managed OAuth for Notion, so you can start there. Build your own public connection only if you need your own client ID and secret, your own branding or redirect URI, or a Marketplace listing. Internal connections and personal access tokens use static tokens and skip OAuth.

steps.title: Confirm you can create connections
steps.detail: Check that your account has the Workspace Owner role in the target workspace. Notion's internal-connection page states this requirement; its public-connection page does not, so confirm it with Notion. Also confirm whether a paid plan or partner program is needed.
gotchas: The public-connection docs do not state the Workspace Owner requirement, so treat it as likely but unconfirmed.

steps.title: Create the public connection
steps.detail: Open the Developer portal, go to the Build section, and choose Public connections. Click Create new connection and fill in the connection name, development workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope, and capabilities. A community guide also lists owner or contact details, privacy policy, and terms as fields.

values.label: Installation scope
values.value: Any workspace (Marketplace-eligible) or Selected workspaces only (not Marketplace-eligible). Decide now: it cannot be changed later.

gotchas: Installation scope is set at creation and cannot be changed. Choose Any workspace now if you may want a Marketplace listing.
The legacy notion.so/my-integrations URL redirects to the developer portal, which renders as a JavaScript-only page. If the form does not appear, reload with JavaScript enabled.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the redirect URI field of the connection, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. Notion sends users back to this URI with a temporary code after they grant access. A community guide says URIs cannot contain fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or public IP addresses; verify this against current docs.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: If more than one redirect URI is configured, redirect_uri is required in the token request.
Redirect URIs must match exactly what you send in the authorize and token requests.

steps.title: Choose capabilities deliberately
steps.detail: Select only the content, comment, and user-information capabilities the agent needs. Notion shows users a consent prompt describing these before the page picker. Changing capabilities later forces existing users to re-authenticate.
gotchas: Email-level user information is the broadest user access option.
Public connections alone can create workspace-level pages and databases by omitting the parent field.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: Open the connection and go to the Configuration tab. Copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret. Store the secret in your secret manager, not in source code. Enter both in your Composio auth config for Notion.
gotchas: How Composio accepts custom client credentials was not verified in this research; check the Composio auth config screen.

steps.title: Build the authorization URL and run a test authorization
steps.detail: Try the Authorization URL shown on the connection. Notion says this field fills in only after submission for review. If it is empty, build the URL yourself with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user, and an optional state value. Open it in a browser signed in to a test workspace and approve access with your own account.
gotchas: Whether a hand-built URL works before submission is not confirmed by the docs. Test it and record the result.
Each user must complete the flow individually.

steps.title: Verify the token exchange
steps.detail: POST the authorization code to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token with HTTP Basic authentication (client ID and secret) and a JSON body using grant_type=authorization_code and the code. Include redirect_uri if it was in the authorize URL or if more than one redirect URI is configured. Confirm the response contains an access token and a refresh token.
gotchas: Access token lifetime is not stated in the fetched pages; measure it during testing.

steps.title: Implement token storage and refresh
steps.detail: Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token. Each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token, so save the full token pair after every successful authorization or refresh. Discard the old refresh token once the new pair is stored.
gotchas: Storing only the access token or keeping the old refresh token will break refresh on the next cycle.

steps.title: Test with invited users in a test workspace
steps.detail: Keep the development connection limited to test workspaces. Invite test users and have each one complete the authorization flow individually. Handle HTTP 429 and 529 responses and respect Retry-After, because rate limits apply per connection.
gotchas: Notion documents no test-user allowlist or install cap; the limit here is only that each user must authorize individually.
Rate limits may change; Notion says it plans to adjust them.

steps.title: Draft listing and compliance materials
steps.detail: Draft the listing name, description, category, tags, and logo text, plus a privacy policy, terms, and owner or contact details, for your review. Read Notion's Connection Gallery best-practices guide before drafting, since it was not reviewed in this research. Check that the connection is Any workspace scope.
gotchas: The privacy policy and terms requirement comes only from a third-party guide; confirm with Notion.
Images and logo specs, and any demo video, are not stated in the findings.

steps.title: Submit the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: In the Listings > Connections dashboard, complete the listing with the linked public connection and submit it to Notion's team for review. Notion says the connection must pass a security review before listing.
gotchas: Only Any workspace connections are eligible. A Selected workspaces only connection cannot be listed.
Submitting may also populate the Authorization URL field (see the Gate 1 step).

steps.title: Wait for the review decision
steps.detail: Notion says to expect an email within 5-10 business days of submission. Track status on the Listings > Connections page. If rejected, read the emailed reason, revise the connection, and resubmit.
gotchas: Rejection can be for brand or trademark issues, quality, or failure to meet baseline criteria.

requirements.item: Workspace Owner role to create a connection
requirements.detail: Stated on Notion's internal-connection page. Not stated on the public-connection page; confirm before relying on it.
Enter redirect URIs at creation. Community guidance: must have a protocol; no fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or public IP addresses. Verify against current docs.
Required when it was passed in the authorize URL or when more than one redirect URI is configured.
Notion describes public connections as following OAuth 2.0. PKCE is not mentioned in the fetched pages, so do not assume it is supported.

requirements.item: Token pair stored on every response
requirements.detail: Refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token. Store the pair after every successful authorization or refresh.
Each user gets an individual token and must complete the flow individually.

180 requests per minute on non-Business plans; 600 per minute on Business and Enterprise; separate shared per-workspace limit. Handle 429 and 529 and respect Retry-After. No special cap for new connections found.
Public connections must pass a Notion security review before they can be listed. Review depth is not stated.

requirements.item: Any workspace installation scope for listing
requirements.detail: Only Any workspace public connections can be listed.
Email reply within 5-10 business days of submission.
Community guide says these are required in the public-connection setup. Not confirmed in Notion's own docs.

scopes.effect: Control which page and database endpoints the connection can call. Notion does not name any content capability as restricted. Request only what you need, because fewer capabilities make workspace admin install more likely.
Control comment endpoint access. Not named as restricted. Adding or removing this later forces users to re-authenticate.

scopes.scope: User information: none, without email, with email
scopes.effect: Email-level access is the broadest user access option. Notion does not name it as restricted, but expect closer reviewer attention to user data in a Marketplace listing (inferred, not stated in docs).
Changing capabilities requires existing users to re-authenticate, so plan capabilities before the first install.

blockers.symptom: The Authorization URL field on the connection is empty, so there is no hosted URL to test with.
blockers.cause: Notion says the field populates only after the public connection is submitted for review.
blockers.fix: Build the authorize URL from the documented parameters (client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user). Test it. If it does not work before submission, submit the listing or contact Notion before relying on the flow.

blockers.cause: Notion lists brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, and failure to meet baseline connection criteria as rejection reasons.
blockers.fix: Read the reason in Notion's email, revise the connection and listing, and resubmit. Check brand names and logo before first submission.

blockers.symptom: Want a Marketplace listing but the connection was created as Selected workspaces only.
blockers.cause: Installation scope is fixed at creation. Selected workspaces only connections are not Marketplace-eligible, and the scope cannot be changed.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with Any workspace installation scope and move the listing work to it.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Notion OAuth app. Its default redirect is Composio's backend callback, and it lists an empty scope list because Notion uses capabilities, not OAuth scope strings. Move to your own public connection only if you need your own client ID and secret, custom branding or redirect URI, or a Marketplace listing. Internal connections and personal access tokens skip OAuth entirely.
